newsitem.title: FRANCE: ETA rebels targeted French leaders.
newsitem.headline: ETA rebels targeted French leaders.

text.p: The Spanish Basque separatist group ETA plotted to kill French Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre and his predecessor Charles Pasqua, according to a hitlist found by French police this week, a justice source said on Friday.
The list was found in a cache of documents police uncovered when they arrested suspected guerrilla leader Juan Luis Aguirre Lete in Bayonne near the Franco-Spanish border on Tuesday, the source said.
Also on the hitlist were magistrate Laurence Le Vert and senior police officer Roger Marion, both in charge of investigations into ETA's activities in France, he said.

Aguirre, suspected of having ordered an foiled attempt to kill King Juan Carlos last year, was due to be brought before an investigating magistrate in Paris at a remand hearing later on Friday, along with his companion, a German woman whose name was not released, the source told Reuters.
The Spanish government applauded his arrest, saying it had led directly to the dismantling of a guerrilla squad on Friday that had been planning attacks in the Navarre region of Spain.
Aguirre's arrest followed that earlier in the week of Juan Insausti Mugica, codenamed Karpov, another suspected ETA leader, held in the southwest France city of Bordeaux.
Their arrests were the latest by France following increased cooperation between French and Spanish police, especially since new conservative governments took office in both countries.

The French newspaper Le Monde said the hitlist indicated a change in strategy by ETA which has generally avoided operating in France, preferring to use the country as a staging area for its operations into neighbouring Spain.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed some 800 people in the 28 years it has been struggling for Basque independence.
